items.instructions: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to the word on the left.

items.prompt: pay

explanation.en: Pay and salary both mean the money you get for your work; a salary is usually paid monthly.

items.prompt: worker

explanation.en: An employee is a person who works for a company and is paid by it.

items.prompt: client

explanation.en: A customer buys goods or services from a shop or a company, so client is a close synonym.

items.prompt: chief

explanation.en: Your boss is the person in charge of you at work.
explanation.es: Boss es informal; chief suena más serio.

items.prompt: personnel

explanation.en: Personnel is the formal word for all the people who work somewhere; staff is the everyday word.
explanation.es: Staff es colectivo: a member of staff, no "a staff".

items.instructions: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to the word on the left.

items.prompt: baggage

explanation.en: Luggage is the usual British word; baggage means the same.
explanation.es: Luggage no tiene plural: two pieces of luggage.

items.prompt: day out

explanation.en: A trip is a short journey to a place and back, like a day out.

items.prompt: overseas

explanation.en: Abroad means in or to another country, like overseas.
explanation.es: Se dice go abroad, sin preposición.

items.prompt: visitor (on holiday)

explanation.en: A tourist is a visitor who is on holiday in a place.

items.prompt: voyage

explanation.en: A voyage is a long journey, and journey is the everyday word.

items.prompt: work that a teacher asks you to do at home

explanation.en: Homework is done at home, after lessons.

items.prompt: a test of what you know, on paper or spoken

explanation.en: You take an exam to show what you have learnt.

items.prompt: a child or young person who goes to school

explanation.en: Pupil is the usual word for a child at school; student is also used for older learners.

items.prompt: the room where a teacher gives lessons

explanation.en: A classroom is the room in a school where lessons happen.

explanation.en: You stop or slow down at a junction before you go on.

items.prompt: a person who walks in the street, not in a car

explanation.en: Pedestrians use the pavement and the crossings.

items.prompt: a large open area in a town, with buildings around it

explanation.en: Many towns have a main square with cafés and a market.

items.prompt: a structure that takes a road or a railway over a river

explanation.en: A bridge lets you cross a river without getting wet.

items.prompt: Keep the ___ in case you want to take the jumper back to the shop.

explanation.en: A receipt is the paper that proves you paid.

items.prompt: There is a twenty per cent ___ on all winter coats this week.

explanation.en: A discount is a lower price than usual.

items.prompt: The ___ scanned my shopping at the till and told me the total.

explanation.en: A cashier takes the money at a shop till.

items.prompt: I put the milk and the bread in the ___ and went to the till.

explanation.en: In a British supermarket you push a trolley.
explanation.es: Trolley es el carro de la compra; en inglés americano, cart.

items.prompt: We waited in a long ___ at the post office to send the parcel.

explanation.en: A queue is a line of people who wait, one behind another.

items.instructions: Complete each sentence with the best word.

items.prompt: I have a terrible ___ and the bright light makes it worse.

explanation.en: A headache is a pain in your head.

items.prompt: Take this ___ after your meals, three times a day.

explanation.en: Medicine is what you take to treat an illness.
explanation.es: Medicine es el medicamento, no el médico (doctor).

items.prompt: She has a high ___ and feels hot and shivery.

explanation.en: A fever is a body temperature higher than normal.

items.prompt: I have had a dry ___ all week and my throat hurts.

explanation.en: A dry cough makes you push air out noisily without any liquid.

items.prompt: Our team is playing a football ___ against the other school on Saturday.

explanation.en: A match is a game between two teams or players.
